context: Tests whether the agent adds a Diagram placeholder with embedded D2 source when the transcript describes a multi-component architecture or request flow that prose alone cannot clarify. Also verifies independent numbering (Diagram counter separate from Screenshot, Code, Link, Fact), a VERIFY comment on the diagram, the draft-summary reporting Diagram counts, and editorial judgement about when a diagram earns its place.

checklist.name: Draft file naming
checklist.description: A file named blog-draft-per-tenant-rate-limiter.md exists in the working directory

checklist.name: Diagram placeholder present
checklist.description: The draft contains at least one Diagram placeholder using the format [Diagram NN: description] where NN is zero-padded (e.g., [Diagram 01: request flow through the rate limiter middleware])

checklist.name: Diagram has D2 source block
checklist.description: The Diagram placeholder is immediately followed (after the bracketed line) by a fenced code block tagged as d2 (```d2 ... ```) containing diagram source code, not just a placeholder description

checklist.name: D2 source reflects transcript components
checklist.description: The D2 source references the actual components described in the transcript: at minimum the client/edge load balancer, the rate-limiter middleware, Redis, and the API. A control-plane node is a plus but not required. The source is not a generic placeholder diagram.

checklist.name: Diagram VERIFY comment
checklist.description: The Diagram placeholder block includes a VERIFY HTML comment indicating the diagram was reconstructed from narrative context (e.g., <!-- VERIFY: diagram reconstructed from narrative context, confirm architecture -->)

checklist.name: Diagram placed in the flow section
checklist.description: The Diagram placeholder appears inside the section that explains the request flow or architecture (the section describing how client, middleware, Redis, and API interact), NOT in the opening hook or the author bio

checklist.name: Independent numbering preserved
checklist.description: The Diagram counter is independent of Screenshot, Code, Link, and Fact counters. If the draft contains Screenshot 01, Code 01, and Diagram 01, all three coexist starting at 01. The draft does NOT use a shared counter across types (e.g., Screenshot 01, Code 02, Diagram 03 where 03 reflects a shared total).

checklist.name: Draft summary counts diagrams
checklist.description: draft-summary.md (or the equivalent conversational summary produced with the deliverables) lists Diagram placeholder count alongside Screenshot, Code, Link, and Fact counts

checklist.name: Screenshot placeholders still used where appropriate
checklist.description: The draft retains Screenshot placeholders for the concrete artifacts Mira pulled up in the transcript (the middleware config file and the Grafana dashboard) instead of replacing every visual with a diagram

checklist.name: Code VERIFY comment present
checklist.description: At least one Code placeholder or reconstructed code block includes a VERIFY comment (the Redis INCR key pattern or the middleware config are natural candidates)

checklist.name: Opening is narrative
checklist.description: The first section after the TLDR opens with a story or specific moment (Mira's onboarding-tenant bug, Dev's earlier failure, or the big-customer-DDoS-by-accident scenario), NOT a thesis statement or a 'In this post we will explore' preamble

checklist.name: TLDR is bullets
checklist.description: The draft contains a TLDR section that uses 2-4 bullet points (lines starting with - or *), placed before the opening hook, not prose paragraphs

checklist.name: Dev appears as recurring character
checklist.description: Dev (the recurring character from the voice profile and transcript) appears in the draft with dialogue, reaction, or a quoted prior-experience aside -- not merely named in passing

checklist.name: Bio post-specific kicker
checklist.description: The draft ends with an author bio for Mira Okafor whose rotating kicker (final sentence) references something specific from THIS post (e.g., 429s, fail-closed, sliding windows, Redis failover)

checklist.name: No preamble announcement
checklist.description: The draft does NOT contain phrases like 'In this post, we will', 'Let's explore', 'What follows is', or 'Let's take a look at'

checklist.name: Word count range
checklist.description: The blog post body (excluding the author bio section) contains between 1,500 and 2,200 words
